summary: Asgard on Aenor Isle: the four isle houses and their queen, harbours and the western lanes, the sea watch, a loyal crown and the western sails.

house_moot.name: The House-Moot
house_moot.desc: Four houses, one moot, and a queen chosen by consent.

house_moot_2.name: The Queen's Peace
house_moot_2.desc: No house seizes another's ship and no quarrel is carried onto the quays.

house_ledgers.name: The House Ledgers
house_ledgers.desc: The houses audit one another each spring: tedious and extraordinarily effective.

isle_fisheries.name: The Fishing Fleets
isle_fisheries.desc: Half the isle eats from the sea, and the other half sells to those who do.

western_lanes.name: The Western Lanes
western_lanes.desc: Steersmen who know the sea-lanes to the West Lands mile by mile.

isle_fleet.name: The Isle Fleet
isle_fleet.desc: Galleys, warships and guide-boats under the Queen's own flag.

sea_watch.name: The Sea Watch
sea_watch.desc: Watchers on the headlands scan the horizon day and night.

sea_watch_2.name: The Isle Stands
sea_watch_2.desc: Beacon, wall and fleet joined into a single system.

loyal_isle.name: The Loyal Isle
loyal_isle.desc: The Concord Council has named Asgard the Loyal Isle.

western_sails.name: The Western Sails
western_sails.desc: Sails on the western horizon: the beacons are lit and the chains are raised.

isle_spared.name: The Isle Spared
isle_spared.desc: The harbours were opened to spare the towns, and the people are not sure whether to be proud.

the_house_moot.title: The House-Moot
the_house_moot.desc: The four houses of Asgard have assembled in the moot-hall, and each has sent a speaker with a different concern. Queen Faberra must decide which of the three to hear first, and the other two will remember.

options.name: House Holod speaks for the purse.
House Rish speaks for the crown.

chapel_by_the_harbour.title: A Chapel by the Harbour
chapel_by_the_harbour.desc: A chapel of the First Light has been raised beside the harbour, and the almoners ask the Queen to bless the fleet there in the Deliverer's name. The sailors do not mind, and the old fishermen do not entirely like it.

options.name: The sea keeps its own gods.
Bless the fleet in the Deliverer's name.

focuses.name: The Isle Houses
focuses.desc: Queen Faberra sits in the house-moot with the lords of four old houses: Rish, Tinta, Holod and Faber. They have ruled Aenor Isle together since the first Aenoran ships dropped anchor.

focuses.name: The Four Houses
focuses.desc: Each of the four houses keeps a seat in the moot, a ship in the harbour and a long memory of the others' errors. The Queen is chosen from among them and rules by consent.

focuses.name: The First Port
focuses.desc: Asgard was the first port Aenoran ships reached, and its houses have never let anyone forget it. The crown thanks them for it, in its fashion.

focuses.name: The Queen's Peace
focuses.desc: Queen Faberra lays her peace on the isle: no house shall seize another's ship, and no quarrel shall be carried onto the quays.

focuses.name: Chapels by the Harbour
focuses.desc: Chapels have begun to appear by the harbour, small, white and open at all hours. The Houses of the First Light bless the departing ships, and the sailors do not object.

focuses.name: The House Ledgers
focuses.desc: The four houses agree to keep their books in the same hand, and to audit one another each spring. It is expensive, tedious and extraordinarily effective.

focuses.name: One Isle, One Queen
focuses.desc: The four houses declare that the isle has one queen and one law. The house-moot sits in the same hall, and its seats are a little closer together.

focuses.name: Harbours of the Isle
focuses.desc: The isle's harbours are deepened and walled, and the old quays are rebuilt in stone. A hundred ships may lie here in any wind.

focuses.name: The Fishing Fleets
focuses.desc: The isle's fleets put out at dawn and return at dusk, their holds full of silver fish. Half the isle eats from the sea, and the other half sells to those who do.

focuses.name: Isle Shipwrights
focuses.desc: The isle's shipwrights build the sturdiest hulls in the central sea, on slips of black oak that were old when the first Aenoran landed.

focuses.name: The Western Lanes
focuses.desc: Asgard's steersmen know the sea-lanes to the West Lands, mile by mile, and sell the knowledge to anyone who can afford it. The western courts trade here, and resent Aenor's tariffs.

focuses.name: Charts of the Central Sea
focuses.desc: The isle's steersmen draw charts of the central sea, with every current, shoal and wreck set down in a clear hand. Such charts are worth more than the ships that sail by them.

focuses.name: The Isle Galleys
focuses.desc: Long oared galleys are built on the isle's slips, fast and shallow, for the patrol of the coast and the escort of merchant fleets.

focuses.name: Warehouses of Asgard
focuses.desc: Great warehouses line the harbour, stocked with the goods of two coasts. A merchant who wants anything in the central sea begins his search here.

focuses.name: The Isle Fleet
focuses.desc: The isle's galleys, warships and guide-boats are joined into a single fleet under the Queen's own flag. It is not a large navy, but it is very well informed.

focuses.name: The Sea Watch
focuses.desc: Watchers on the headlands scan the horizon day and night. Any sail, any smoke, any change in the colour of the water is reported to the Queen before noon.

focuses.name: Lighthouses
focuses.desc: Tall stone lighthouses are raised on the western headlands, each with a fire-basket and a watch-room. They warn friends and mark the isle for strangers.

focuses.name: The Western Beacons
focuses.desc: Beacons are raised along the western shore, each a bow-shot from the next. A flame at the isle's tip is seen on the mainland within the hour.

focuses.name: Sea Soldiers
focuses.desc: The isle schools its own sea soldiers, men who fight from the deck and the quay with equal ease. They wear leather, carry short blades and do not fear the water.

focuses.name: Harbour Chains
focuses.desc: Great iron chains are laid across the harbour mouths, to be raised with a capstan when a strange sail is sighted. A fleet that wishes to land must first break them.

effects.tooltip: Chains across the harbour slow a landing.

focuses.name: The Isle Garrison
focuses.desc: A permanent garrison is raised for the isle, drawn from the four houses in equal numbers. It is the only army on Aenor Isle, and it is not small.

focuses.name: The Isle Stands
focuses.desc: The isle's defences are joined into a single system of beacon, wall and fleet. If the central sea should ever bring a host to these shores, the isle will stand.

focuses.name: Crown and Isle
focuses.desc: Asgard is the Concord's most loyal dominion, and its houses make a point of saying so at every gathering. The loyalty is genuine, and it is rewarded.

focuses.name: Ships for the King's Fleet
focuses.desc: The isle's shipwrights build for the Golden King's fleet, and the isle's steersmen lead it across the wide central sea. The Golden Court pays promptly, which is rare enough to be noted.

focuses.name: The Isle Charter Confirmed
focuses.desc: The Old Charter of the isle is read aloud in the moot and confirmed by all four houses. The Queen signs, the lords seal, and the crown is informed.

focuses.name: Isle Lords at Parim
focuses.desc: The four lords of the isle travel to Parim for the Concord Council, in their best robes and their worst tempers. They return with promises and a new respect for distance.

focuses.name: The Loyal Isle
focuses.desc: The Concord Council names Asgard the Loyal Isle, and the title is carved over the harbour gate. The islanders pretend not to notice.

focuses.name: The Western Sails
focuses.desc: Sails on the western horizon, hundreds of them, and not one of them flies a friend's colours. The beacons are lit and the chains are raised.

focuses.name: Bar the Harbours
focuses.desc: The harbours are shut with chains and ships. If the fleet of the West is to land, it will have to land somewhere else, and the Queen has made it clear where she would prefer.

focuses.name: Spare the Isle
focuses.desc: The Queen opens the harbours to spare her towns the fire. Her sailors are ashamed and her merchants are relieved, and the history of the isle is rewritten in a single afternoon.

focuses.name: The Isle Rises
focuses.desc: Every fisherman and every dockhand takes up a spear. The isle has not been invaded in living memory, and its people have no intention of losing the habit.

focuses.name: Harbours for the Heir
focuses.desc: The Heir has returned, and the isle's harbours are opened to him and his ships. The Queen gives him the best steersmen she has.

focuses.name: The Isle Rebuilt
focuses.desc: The sails are gone and the isle begins to mend. The harbours are cleared, the quays rebuilt and the first fishing-boat puts out at dawn, as if nothing had happened.

focuses.name: The Tide-Chambers Opened
focuses.desc: Under Borrak the old halls are cut into the last hill of rock, and the sea fills them at every high water. The queen orders them pumped and lit at low tide, and the isle houses store their grain where their great-grandmothers held their moots.

focuses.name: Nets of Field-Stone Kept
focuses.desc: The fishers of the western shore bring up quern-stones and the footings of field walls in their nets, and they have always thrown them back. The queen asks them to bring the stones ashore instead and give them to the old women of the houses.

focuses.name: The Queens' Rite
focuses.desc: The rite of the tide-chamber belongs to the isle houses alone, and two claimants have come asking to share it: the crown at Parim and the Orran mothers of the downs. The queens will give it to one of them and never to both.

focuses.name: Divers of Borrak
focuses.desc: The houses school divers on the long swims between the chamber mouths, where a breath held too long is the only mistake a diver makes once. The best of them can work a full minute on the bottom at slack water.

focuses.name: The Mound at Low Water
focuses.desc: At the lowest spring tides a reef of cut stone breaks the water west of the isle, and the oldest women of the houses call it the Mothers' Mound. The queen means to send her own divers down to it under her own flag.
